text:
anya: quick sync — we need a concrete decision on v1 sunsetting. telemetry shows ~5% of production traffic still hitting v1 endpoints, and a handful of enterprise customers on pinned clients. propose: 6-month deprecation window, default routing of unknown clients to v2 with a compatibility fallthrough header, and a console banner + quota warnings. thoughts?

matt: 5% seems high but not unexpected. question: do we force 301-style reject after X months, or keep a fallback routing for extra time?

oliver: prefer a staged approach. month 0-2: soft banner + telemetry sampling that injects compatibility flags; month 2-4: route v1 -> v2 with automatic translation for known safe paths; month 4-6: block write endpoints, keep read-only for a grace period, then hard-block.

anya: sounds reasonable. main risk is silent failures for customers using undocumented headers. we need a safe translation layer for the most common headers/body shapes.

vikas: can infra handle on-the-fly translation for heavy paths? translation will add latency. maybe only translation for small fraction (canary) and telemetry to decide next steps.

infra-bot: deploy:compat-proxy v1.2 rolled to canary (10% infra) at 2024-11-07T10:22Z — logs show +12ms p99 on sample.

matt: +12ms p99 is acceptable if we keep canary low and monitor. but we should be explicit in docs: translation may change tokenization for some models, risk of subtle quality diffs.

anya: good point. add a quality regression gate to rollout. we need alerting on: 1) increase in error rates after translation 2) increase in downstream latency 3) customer-reported mismatches.

oliver: for the console UX: propose per-tenant banner that shows "Your app is calling v1 (5% of traffic). Migrate to v2 — click to see migration steps" with a link to a migration checklist. also surface quota impact and any required header changes.

vikaS (typo): (reaction :eyes:)

vikas: also think about routing policy for dedicated customers on Dedicated clusters. they may prefer a config toggle to keep v1 behavior on for longer. need to wire per-customer policy with SLA guardrails.

anya: yes — Dedicated should have an override flag in the console: 
```
policy:
  api_compat_mode: preserve_v1
  expiry: 2025-05-01T00:00:00Z
```
console will warn about security/maintenance exposures.

matt: telemetry gap: we don't have full visibility into SDK versions and user agent strings for some customers because of proxy masking. need to add sticky client-id header in the proxy to capture SDK version when available. a transient header like `X-Client-SDK: redwood-js@0.18.2` would help.

oliver: agreed. also add a heuristic: if no client id, check request shape/timeouts to infer likely v1 clients (low-attention to new fields). that should go into the migration scoring.

anya: for deprecation notices: 1) email owners with >0.1% traffic, 2) console banner when >0.01% 3) public changelog + API status page. set cadence: 90d, 60d, 30d, 14d, 7d, 1d.

vikas: enforcement options: block with 403, redirect with 307 to v2, or transparent translation. which do we standardize? prefer translation for first 2 months, then 307 with clear error payload including `upgrade_required: true` field.

anya: agreed. error payload example we can standardize: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "api_version_deprecated",
  "message": "v1 will be removed on 2025-05-01. See https://console.redwood.ai/migrate for migration steps.",
  "upgrade_required": true,
  "doc_link": "https://console.redwood.ai/migrate"
}
```

oliver: UX nuance: customers like interactive migration help. Can we add an automated migration assistant in console that scans their recent requests and highlights incompatible fields?

matt: that would be powerful. technically we can replay sampled requests through a v2 translator in a sandbox and show diffs. need to respect PII — must run in customer's account or anonymize payloads.

anya: please add to privacy checklist. also add a telemetry metric: `migration_sandbox_diffs_percent` to measure how many requests changed shape. we will use that to estimate migration effort.

infra-bot: alert rule created: compat-translation-errors > 1% for 5m -> notify #incidents and ping oncall.

vikas: final ask: CLI/SDKs should default to v2 after we announce but keep `REDWOOD_API_VERSION=1` env override for 180 days. call that an escape hatch.

anya: OK. action items I captured: 
- infra: keep canary at 10%, telemetry gating (+12ms p99 accept threshold) (assignee: oliver)
- platform: implement standardized 403 error payload and console banner + per-tenant override (assignee: matt)
- devex: add SDK env override + default to v2 + add client-id header (assignee: vikas)
- product: migration assistant feasibility and privacy checklist (assignee: sara)
- infra-bot: ensure alerts for translation errors (already created)

please ack and I’ll open a ticket that consolidates these into a rollout plan. :thumbsup:

sara: acked, will scope the migration assistant and privacy requirements.

oliver: ack, will keep canary and post perf numbers every morning.

matt: ack, will spec the console copy and API error contract.

vikas: ack, will ship SDK default and header.

anya: thanks everyone — I’ll create the rollout RFC + timeline.

infra-bot: ticket created: RFC-2025-01-v1-sunset (link: https://redwood.internal/r/1234)
